themes.0.1.0: A pass means the question was answered
themes.0.2.0: The key read through panschema's model

items.title: "None on record" only where it's true
items.blurb: An attempt that says "none on record" for a question whose answer is on record fails. The baseline never says it: which records a negative is about is written in the key, not the question.

acceptance.criterion: An attempt that says "none on record" for a question whose answer is on record fails
The baseline never says "none on record"
The baseline fails only closed-world negatives, and only their own check

items.title: Grade a graph published as several files
items.blurb: baseline --graph can repeat, so a schema that publishes one Turtle file per dataset no longer has to be concatenated first.

acceptance.criterion: --graph may be given more than once, and every file loads into one store
A graph split across files retrieves the same as the whole

items.title: A trace names the graph it was run over
items.blurb: A trace records the dataset and version it retrieved over, and grading refuses one whose dataset or version is not the benchmark's target, so a trace from an older graph is not graded against the current key.

acceptance.criterion: A trace whose dataset or version differs from the benchmark's target is refused with exit code 2
The baseline records the dataset and version of the graph it was given, never the benchmark's

items.title: Tell an unanswered negative from a wrong answer
items.blurb: An attempt that reaches a negative's records and says nothing has left it unanswered; one that says "none on record" where the answer is on record is wrong. Grading reports the two apart, so a CI can require no wrong answers from a system that, like the baseline, leaves negatives unanswered.

acceptance.criterion: A negative reached and left unanswered is reported apart from a wrong answer
Grading can require no wrong answers, and the baseline over wine meets it
Any wrong answer still fails that requirement

items.title: A retrieval budget
items.blurb: Anchors must be reached within a cap on how many records are retrieved, so retrieving the whole graph stops passing. Waits on cqa v0.2 deciding whether the cap is the benchmark's to state.

acceptance.criterion: An attempt that retrieves more than the budget fails anchors-reached

items.title: Citation precision
items.blurb: Citing everything that was retrieved stops passing attribution. Waits on cqa v0.2, for the same reason: who sets the floor.

acceptance.criterion: Attribution fails when the share of citations the key expects is under the floor

items.title: Check the answer, not only its evidence
items.blurb: Where cqa declares an expected value for an answer kind (a lookup's value, a comparison's order, a quantity within a tolerance), the kind's check compares it with the attempt's, so reaching the right records and answering wrongly fails. The trace gains a structured answer to compare. Waits on cqa v0.2, which scopes expected values.

acceptance.criterion: A lookup whose answer is not the expected value fails, though it reached every anchor

items.title: Alternative evidence sets
items.blurb: More than one set of records can support some answers; any one set satisfies the anchors, so a correct answer resting on other evidence than the key's first choice passes. Waits on cqa declaring them, which its v0.2 scope does not yet include.

acceptance.criterion: An attempt that reaches any one of a question's evidence sets reaches its anchors

items.title: Read the answer key from its source
items.blurb: The key is read from the benchmark's YAML, through panschema's model of the cqa schema, instead of from its Turtle rendering.

acceptance.criterion: The YAML and Turtle readers give the same benchmark for wine

items.title: Baseline traversal through panschema
items.blurb: The baseline looks up neighboring records with panschema's subgraph search instead of its own SPARQL queries.

items.title: Judging the answer
items.blurb: The second tier: the prose answer judged against ground_truth, behind a flag and out of CI.

items.title: Scores across a benchmark
items.blurb: Mean recall and precision over every question, so a retriever's progress shows as one number per run.

items.title: Ranked retrieval
items.blurb: A trace that orders what it retrieved, for measures like MRR and nDCG that reward putting the anchors first. A trace is a set today, so this changes the format.
